items.title: Carmen Leggio interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: And so we used to play all over... That’s when I realized that something was happening with me. And so we used to play all over... But then when I picked up the tenor and we played this Club Six and it was Primo, June Bug and myself.

ctx.x: And you took up the tenor after that?

Clarinet about ten years old, nine years old; tenor fourteen. And there was a bass player called Primo Rico that was in town, and we used to have little things going on with the clarinet and so on, little groups. And he went up to my mother and told her to please get me a tenor because he saw something in me. So that’s when they got me a tenor, my © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

father and my mother, and I just picked it up and blew it with the radio, and played with groups around town. Westchester was very big with music, very big. Every place you turned there was music going on.
